concepts.name: Health report
concepts.definition: A structured record NICo attaches to a host, rack, switch or other object, listing failed checks as alerts and passed checks as successes, each tagged with a source.

concepts.name: Health probe ID
concepts.definition: A stable identifier for one specific health check, for example BmcSensor or HeartbeatTimeout, used to label alerts and successes in health reports.

concepts.name: Health alert classification
concepts.definition: A conventional tag on a health alert, for example PreventAllocations, that tells NICo how the alert should affect allocation, state changes or alerting.

concepts.name: PreventAllocations
concepts.definition: A classification that stops tenants from getting the host as an instance, unless targeted instance creation is used.

concepts.name: PreventHostStateChanges
concepts.definition: A classification that keeps a host from moving between certain lifecycle states while it is unclear whether all required configuration has been applied.

concepts.name: SuppressExternalAlerting
concepts.definition: A classification that leaves a host out of the site-wide fleet-health calculation, so known issues do not trigger external alerts.

concepts.name: Merge vs Replace health reports
concepts.definition: Two ways a source can write a health report. A Merge report is combined with the host's other reports. A Replace report overrides them and takes precedence.

concepts.name: Aggregate host health
concepts.definition: The combined health of a host, built from all its health report sources. It decides whether classifications such as PreventAllocations apply.

concepts.name: Alert debouncing
concepts.definition: Raising an alert only after a set number of consecutive failed checks, and clearing it on the first success, so short blips are not reported.

concepts.name: NICo state machine
concepts.definition: NICo's controller that moves hosts through lifecycle states such as ingestion, ready and assigned. It also performs automatic recovery actions such as reboots.

concepts.name: Managed Host
concepts.definition: A bare-metal machine (host plus its DPUs) that NICo has ingested and manages.

concepts.name: Instance
concepts.definition: A host allocated to a tenant. Tenants create instances and later release them.

concepts.name: Tenant
concepts.definition: A customer organization that allocates hosts as instances and owns resources such as key groups.

concepts.name: Targeted instance creation
concepts.definition: Creating an instance on a specific Machine ID. In some cases this can bypass health-based allocation blocks.

concepts.name: Baseboard Management Controller (BMC)
concepts.definition: An out-of-band management chip on a server. It reports power state, sensors and events, and allows remote control.

concepts.name: Redfish API
concepts.definition: A standard REST API that BMCs expose for hardware management. NICo uses it, for example, to read leak detectors.

concepts.name: BMC sensor thresholds
concepts.definition: Ranges that a sensor reports: caution, critical, fatal and valid min/max. nico-hardware-health maps them to the SensorWarning, SensorCritical, SensorFatal and SensorFailure classifications.

concepts.name: nico-hardware-health
concepts.definition: The NICo service that reads BMC sensors and events and reports hardware health, such as BmcSensor and leak detection.

concepts.name: Site Explorer
concepts.definition: The NICo component that scrapes BMC endpoints to discover hosts and compares them against Expected Machines.

concepts.name: Expected Machines
concepts.definition: A list of the machines (BMC MAC, serial number and so on) that a site is expected to ingest. It is used to check discovered hardware.

concepts.name: Machine validation
concepts.definition: A framework that runs validation tests on hosts and raises alerts when a test fails or cannot be scheduled.

concepts.name: SKU validation
concepts.definition: A workflow that checks a host's hardware against its expected SKU. If it fails, the host cannot be allocated.

concepts.name: Repair workflow
concepts.definition: A flow in which tenants report broken hosts on release, or flag instances for online repair, so an external framework can fix them.

concepts.name: Maintenance mode
concepts.definition: An admin marking that a host is being worked on. It applies PreventAllocations, SuppressExternalAlerting and ExcludeFromStateMachineSla.

concepts.name: Leak detection
concepts.definition: Health processing that turns raw leak observations (from BMC detectors, NVUE switch sensors or the BMS) into derived tray-level and rack-level leak alerts.

concepts.name: Building Management System (BMS)
concepts.definition: Datacenter facility systems. NICo receives their rack leak events through the DSX Exchange consumer.

concepts.name: NVLink
concepts.definition: NVIDIA's high-bandwidth GPU-to-GPU interconnect. In a rack it links GPUs across compute trays through NVLink switches.

concepts.name: NVLink partition
concepts.definition: A group of GPUs that may talk to each other over NVLink. Partitions are assigned per tenant or are tray defaults.

concepts.name: NMX-C
concepts.definition: The NVLink fabric controller that runs on switches. It manages NVLink partitions and reports domain and GPU health.

concepts.name: NMX-T
concepts.definition: The NVLink telemetry listener service that runs on primary switches.

concepts.name: NVLink partition monitor
concepts.definition: A periodic nico-api task that reconciles NVLink partitions with NMX-C. It raises NmxcUnreachable and NvlinkUnhealthy alerts and performs isolation.

concepts.name: NVLink isolation
concepts.definition: Removing all of a host's GPUs from every NVLink partition, triggered by the IsolateFromNvLinkPartitions classification. It is used before a compute tray is moved or replaced.

concepts.name: NVOS / NVUE
concepts.definition: The NVIDIA switch and network operating system (NVOS) and its configuration and state API (NVUE). They are used on switches and in HBN on DPUs.

concepts.name: Switch reachability monitor
concepts.definition: A nico-api task that makes a TCP connection to each ready switch's NVOS and NMX-T ports, and raises debounced unreachable alerts.

concepts.name: Leader lease / work lock
concepts.definition: A mechanism that makes sure only one nico-api replica runs a monitor at a time. When the lease moves to another replica, that replica takes over.

concepts.name: Data Processing Unit (DPU)
concepts.definition: A SmartNIC with its own CPUs, attached to each host. NICo uses it to enforce networking and runs dpu-agent on it.

concepts.name: dpu-agent
concepts.definition: The NICo agent that runs on the DPU. It applies network configuration, checks local services and sends health reports and heartbeats to NICo core.

concepts.name: HBN (Host-Based Networking)
concepts.definition: NVIDIA's containerized routing stack (FRR, DHCP and so on) on the DPU. dpu-agent configures it through ContainerExec or NVUE.

concepts.name: DPF
concepts.definition: A framework that deploys DPU services, such as HBN, DHCP and FMDS, as pods. When DPF is used, dpu-agent takes the NVUE path.

concepts.name: BGP
concepts.definition: The routing protocol that the DPU uses to peer with top-of-rack switches and route servers. FRR is the daemon that implements it.

concepts.name: Top-of-rack (ToR) uplink
concepts.definition: The DPU's physical uplink ports (p0 and p1) to the rack switches. Normal PXE boot requires p0.

concepts.name: DHCP relay/server on DPU
concepts.definition: The DHCP services that run on the DPU and hand out addresses to the host. Their failure raises DhcpRelay and DhcpServer alerts.

concepts.name: PXE boot
concepts.definition: Booting a machine over the network. It relies on DHCP and on the host's p0 uplink.

concepts.name: FMDS (NICo Metadata Service)
concepts.definition: A metadata service that tenant software on an instance can query. It returns the applied configuration, such as InfiniBand GUIDs, and supports configuration scripts.

concepts.name: DPU restricted mode
concepts.definition: A locked-down DPU mode in which the host cannot reconfigure the DPU. NICo raises an alert if the DPU is not running in it.

concepts.name: InfiniBand
concepts.definition: A high-performance, low-latency network fabric made of HCAs and switches. It is used for HPC and AI traffic.

concepts.name: InfiniBand partition
concepts.definition: An isolated group within an InfiniBand fabric. Tenants attach instance interfaces to partitions.

concepts.name: UFM (Unified Fabric Manager)
concepts.definition: NVIDIA's InfiniBand fabric manager. NICo uses it to manage partition membership.

concepts.name: InfiniBand fabric
concepts.definition: A separate InfiniBand network. Each NIC port connects to one fabric, and a host may span several fabrics.

concepts.name: InfiniBand device (NIC port as device)
concepts.definition: A physical PCI function that can send InfiniBand traffic. NICo presents each port of a multi-port NIC as a separate device.

concepts.name: PCI device and slot address
concepts.definition: An address such as 0000:ca:00.0 that identifies a PCI device. NICo sorts by it to map tenant selections to hardware deterministically.

concepts.name: SR-IOV Physical and Virtual Functions
concepts.definition: A PCI feature in which one physical function (PF) can expose several virtual functions (VFs) that appear as additional devices sharing the same hardware.

concepts.name: InfiniBand GUID and LID
concepts.definition: A GUID is the globally unique hardware ID of an InfiniBand port or VF. A LID is the local address that the subnet manager assigns.

concepts.name: Mellanox firmware tools (mlxconfig, mst)
concepts.definition: Command-line tools for inspecting and configuring ConnectX NIC firmware settings, such as link type and the number of VFs. They operate per physical card.

concepts.name: nico-scout
concepts.definition: A tool that runs on a host during discovery, enumerates its hardware (CPUs, GPUs, NICs) and reports it to NICo.

concepts.name: Discovery data
concepts.definition: The hardware details that nico-scout reports and NICo stores in its database, including InfiniBand devices with PCI properties and GUIDs.

concepts.name: Protocol Buffers
concepts.definition: A schema language and serialization format that NICo uses to define API messages such as InfinibandInterface.

concepts.name: Instance type and machine capabilities
concepts.definition: An instance type groups identical machines. Machine capabilities summarize how many components of each kind those machines have, such as InfiniBand devices per fabric.

concepts.name: InstanceInfinibandConfig
concepts.definition: The tenant's InfiniBand configuration for an instance. Each interface selects a device by name, fabric and device_instance, chooses a PF or VF, and names a partition.

concepts.name: Device-instance to hardware mapping
concepts.definition: The rule that turns a tenant's (device, fabric, device_instance) selection into a specific hardware port: matching devices are sorted by PCI slot and the N-th is chosen.

concepts.name: NUMA node
concepts.definition: A CPU and memory locality domain. The NUMA node a device is attached to affects performance between that device and GPUs.

concepts.name: NICo REST API (cloud)
concepts.definition: The cloud-side NICo service that tenants use. It holds the source of truth for things such as key groups and synchronizes them to sites.

concepts.name: NICo site
concepts.definition: A NICo deployment that runs in one datacenter and manages its hosts. It receives configuration from the cloud REST API.

concepts.name: Key group
concepts.definition: A named set of SSH public keys, stored per tenant, that grants access to the SSH console.

concepts.name: Key group synchronization
concepts.definition: The process in which the cloud REST API pushes versioned key group contents to sites, records which version each site holds, and compares versions to find out of sync sites.

concepts.name: Optimistic concurrency with versions
concepts.definition: Each update gets a new version string, and an update can be rejected if the stored version no longer matches. This prevents overwriting another user's concurrent edit.

concepts.name: SSH public keys
concepts.definition: Public keys that authorize a user to log in over SSH. Here they grant access to the host's serial console.

concepts.name: nico-admin-cli
concepts.definition: An operator command-line tool for administering NICo, for example to remove health reports or apply health templates.
